glosses: Distinguished by a unique, particular, or unusual quality.

examples.text: a special episode of a television series

EVERY CHILD IS SPECIAL
An empty and meaningless sentiment. What about every adult? Isn't every adult special? And if not, then at what age does a person go from being special to being not-so-special? And if every adult is also special, then that means all people are special and the idea has no meaning.

glosses: Of particular value or interest; dear; beloved.

examples.text: Everyone is special to someone.

glosses: Of or related to unconventional warfare.

examples.text: special forces, special operations

glosses: Appointed specifically to examine a single event or issue.

glosses: Constituting or relating to a species.

examples.text: Having seven dark spots is a special property unique to Coccinella septempunctata.

examples.text: What do you mean, you don't understand the sign? What are you, special?

glosses: Of, being, or pertaining to sexual intercourse or the genitals.

examples.text: The parents told the kids not to bother them during special time.

glosses: Infused with a drug, especially marijuana; that is an edible.

examples.text: This book will help you to […] • Cook with the confidence that the neighbors won't find out your brownies are 'special' • Never again worry about getting caught growing because someone smelled your garden

glosses: A reduction in consumer cost (usually for a limited time) for items or services rendered; the thing thus sold.

examples.text: We're running a special on turkey for Thanksgiving.
I didn't have much money, so I bought the special.

glosses: A meal offered only at a certain time by a restaurant, not as a standing fixture of the menu; often, one of a rotation of meals systematically offered for a lower price; also often a dish at a nondiscounted price that is seasonal or otherwise exciting or unusual.

examples.text: Today's dinner special is wild salmon, which we don't normally get a chance to offer.
The Tuesday lunch special is our tuna melt on rye.

glosses: Unusual or exceptional episode of a series.

examples.text: Did you see the Christmas special?

glosses: A special constable.

examples.text: And you can't trust a "Special" like the old-time copper when you can't find your way home.

glosses: Anything that is not according to normal practice, plan, or schedule, as an unscheduled run of transportation that is normally scheduled.

examples.text: Thousands came to see the special that carried the President's coffin.

glosses: Any unlicensed medicine produced or obtained for a specific individual patient.
An award, typically a free game, that is made available to the player upon reaching or completing a major objective in a pinball game.
A journalist sent to the scene of an event to report back.
A dispatch sent back by a special correspondent.
A light that illuminates a specific person or thing on the stage.

examples.text: In addition to followspots, there will be three frontlight specials on Autoyokes hung on the truss to provide frontlight specials.

The first is a special—a single lighting instrument that lights a particular spot on the stage. Specials generally have no color, or a more saturated color, allowing them to stand out through other lighting onstage.

glosses: One of certain mixed-breed dogs.

examples.text: Singapore Special;  Darwin special

glosses: A racehorse predicted to win; a sure thing.

examples.text: "How's your horse going to go Fatty?" My replies included, "It's a special." "Get on. It can't be beaten."

glosses: To supervise a patient one-on-one.

examples.text: We have not sent our pupils out on private duty except a very few times, but they have an unusual amount of specialing to do inside.

Seule la France ralentira le processus, avec le création d'une classe de paysans moyens nombreux issue du partage, inégal mais réel, de la terre des privilégiés sous la Révolution.
